guide.frontierhunts.lesson.wind.p4: Thermals: on slopes, air warmed by the sun rises from mid-morning to late afternoon and carries your scent uphill. As the ground cools in the evening, through the night and into early morning, the air sinks and carries it downhill. Rain dampens scent and thermals, and a spray of Scent Cover shrinks your cone for two minutes.
guide.frontierhunts.lesson.wind.p5: Carbon clothing goes under your clothes, not instead of them: right-click a Carbon Hood, Jacket and Trousers (or the one-piece Carbon Scent Suit) and keep your ghillie, camo or furs on top. A full fresh set holds back nearly 90% of your scent from every animal while you stay still and dry. Sweat, running and wet clothes let more through, and the carbon wears out with use: wash it in a stream or air it by the fire. The Field Gear panel beside your inventory shows the layer and how much scent gets out.
guide.frontierhunts.tip.winded.body: That animal smelled you. Keep the wind blowing from it to you; hold the Wind Checker to see your scent cone. A carbon base layer under your clothes keeps most of your scent in.
guide.frontierhunts.tip.cold.body: Get out of the wind: a tent, a cabin or a cave keeps the storm off and holds your warmth, and a fire inside warms you fastest. Tan hides and furs into coats, hats and mukluks; a fur lining fits under your camo. Wet clothes keep you less warm until a fire dries them.
guide.frontierhunts.lesson.tips.p2: Dress in layers. Everything you wear adds warmth: furs and hides the most, then coveralls, ghillie and the thin carbon base layer. Wind and wet clothes take it away, heavy fur gets hot when you run, and the Layers page of the Field Gear panel shows what keeps you warm.
journal.frontierhunts.check.gear_ghillie: Own a ghillie (Frontier Workbench, Clothing) or a carbon base-layer piece (Frontier Workbench, Scent & packs).
onboard.frontierhunts.step.7.p1: Tan hides and furs on a Tanning Rack. At the Frontier Workbench (Clothing tab), turn them into fur hats, coats and boots for the cold, or sew a fur lining into what you wear. Everything you wear adds warmth; wind and wet clothes take it away.
